findings.issue: The health tile's header draws the status chip on the card's START edge and the title (with its icon trailing the text) on the END edge — the exact inverse of the export. Measured live in the host on W12's first tile (card x 761..1106, so start = 1106): chip «سليم» at 1040..1067 (start), title «قاعدة البيانات» at 804..888 and its icon at ~786 (end). The preview (design/exports/preview/{light,dark}/W/W12 — مركز الصحة.jpg) draws icon+title on the START edge and the status chip on the END edge on every tile (e.g. rightmost card x 528..778: db icon at ~762, title to its left, «● سليم» at 545..585). The cause is the markup order in .w-health-head, which emits <WChip> before <span class="w-health-title">, and inside the title the icon after the text. This is repeated on all eleven tiles of W12 in both themes and is the only anatomy deviation left in the package (the footer — timestamp on the start edge, action on the end edge — already matches).
findings.fix: In src/Wakeel.Design/Components/WHealthCard.razor swap the two children of .w-health-head so the <span class="w-health-title"> is emitted first and the <WChip> second (keep .w-health-head's justify-content: space-between in WHealthCard.razor.css untouched), and inside .w-health-title move the <span class="w-health-icon"> block ABOVE the <span class="w-health-title-text">, so the icon leads the title under RTL. Add a bUnit fact next to WHealthCard_PutsTheRunsTimeOnTheStartEdge_... in tests/Wakeel.UI.Tests/Components/DailyShellComponentTests.cs asserting that .w-health-head's first element child is .w-health-title and its second is .w-chip, and re-photograph W12 beside the preview.

HOST RUNS. Two runs, each on a freshly activated temporary data folder seeded through HostDataFolderSeed, Wakeel.Desktop.exe with --remote-debugging-port=9333 --window-size=1366x768 --data-folder=<temp> --start-url=/login, driven over CDP with a 1366x768 device-metrics override. Run 1 (ordinary seed): signed in, photographed W08, W09, W12, W91, W92, the bell panel (W10) and the quick-capture dialog (W94) in dark, then the same set in light through wakeelUi.setTheme. Run 2 (WAKEEL_HOST_SKEW_CLOCK seed): W11 photographed in both themes. Both host logs hold exactly one line, «Wakeel desktop host starting up», and nothing else; both processes killed, zero Wakeel.Desktop processes remain.

LIVE EVIDENCE OF THE WIRING. Ctrl+N dispatched as a real Input.dispatchKeyEvent with the control modifier opened W94 from /w08. The bell panel showed «حان وقت النسخ الاحتياطي · قبل 3 دقائق» — a notification the running host created itself, which is ReminderScheduler under BackgroundPassDispatcher — above the seeded meeting reminder «اجتماع قريب: لجنة المشتريات — عطاء صيانة المركبات». On the skewed folder ClockGuard rendered W11 with its three parts and both buttons, and W12's «ساعة الجهاز» tile agreed with it. No horizontal overflow on any screen (.w-page scrollWidth == clientWidth == 1124 on W08, W09, W12; 712/712 vertically on W91).

SECURITY / RULES. The only MarkupString in src/Wakeel.UI and src/Wakeel.Design is WIcon's, fed from a compile-time IconRegistry lookup — no user data ever becomes markup. Both exports (the health report and W09's list) are written only through IFileSaveService, i.e. a save dialog the person drives, and carry nothing but Arabic sentences. «تصحيح الساعة» launches the compile-time constant ms-settings:dateandtime. Background passes go through ComponentBase.InvokeAsync plus ShellServices' one-at-a-time gate, and the guard and the scheduler are stopped explicitly in LockNow and SignOut before the session scope is disposed. No password, key or token reaches UI state, a log line or a screen. No NuGet package added, no file outside the package's allowed paths touched, and no technical term, error code, port, server or database wording in any Arabic string (the host even drops the export's own «(SQLCipher)» from the database tile's title). Every numeral on every screenshot is a Western digit. A sweep of the icon-only buttons found none without a tooltip; WButton routes every Tooltip through WTooltip and additionally gives the Icon variant its accessible name.
